page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 physical cores and 12 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-core capabilities and weaker single-core execution. The single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is positioned in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, which is mirrored by poor single-threaded gzip compression and weak text processing. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, consistently achieve average performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also fall within the average range, though the Passmark memory score is weak.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU, the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. It is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by average performance in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations at 8.48 million operations per second. The instance is also appropriate for multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, and light LLM inference using small models, but is less optimal for static web serving or single-threaded processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance featuring 12 dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between weak single-core execution and average multi-core capabilities. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing perform poorly, whereas multi-core operations, software compilation, and Redis SET benchmarks achieve average tier results. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from parallel processing rather than raw single-threaded speed. It is best suited for database operations, multi-threaded applications, and small-scale model inference.
